title: Caste Mobilisation and Power in Indian Politics

scenes.text: Do Indians cast their vote or vote their caste in elections?
scenes.narration: Imagine stepping into an Indian election booth. Does democracy destroy ancient caste divisions, or does politics actually give caste a whole new life?

scenes.text: Like school houses joining forces to demand better playground facilities and resources.
scenes.narration: Here is an everyday school analogy to make this click. When students from different grades unite into a team, they gain bargaining power to win real facilities.

scenes.name: M.N. Srinivas
scenes.idea: Caste is not completely rigid because local dominance depends on numbers and land.
scenes.narration: Sociologist M.N. Srinivas showed that caste is not completely rigid. Groups with numbers and land ownership form a dominant caste, gaining real local power.

scenes.heading: Kothari's Politicisation of Caste
scenes.narration: Thinker Rajni Kothari explained that politics changes caste. Instead of ritual purity, caste groups organise to secure secular benefits like education and government jobs.

scenes.heading: Forms of Caste Mobilisation
scenes.narration: Scholars Rudolph and Rudolph noted two mobilisation forms. First, upper castes led lower castes vertically for small concessions, but soon lower castes united horizontally to claim power.

scenes.heading: Plebeianisation and State Politics
items: Christophe Jaffrelot links state formation with caste
Linguistic reorganisation consolidated regional dominant castes
Plebeianisation brings common citizens into political power
Coalition politics reflects rising intermediate caste influence
scenes.narration: Christophe Jaffrelot highlighted plebeianisation, meaning the participation of ordinary people in democracy. Regional coalitions empowered intermediate castes, opening state power beyond traditional elites.

scenes.heading: Impact on Indian Democracy
scenes.narration: Critics like Andre Beteille warn that caste mobilization creates populist divisions. In contrast, scholars like Yogendra Yadav argue it deepens democracy by empowering marginalised citizens.

items: Caste shifted from ritual purity to secular political bargaining
Horizontal mobilisation enabled lower castes to challenge elite power
Plebeianisation and coalitions deepened mass democratic participation
scenes.narration: To recap, caste transformed from rigid ritual hierarchy into a political bargaining tool. Through horizontal solidarity and democratic upsurges, it gave ordinary people a voice.
